thread:
Sylvie: Quick postmortem follow-up from yesterday's cross-region failover test. We identified three recurring patterns (DNS TTL blips, snapshot lag, and route-table drift). I spun up an action list — need owners + timelines. Can people ack and take items?
Alex: Ack. I can own the DNS TTL + canary routing experiment. Suggest a 2-week window for changes behind a canary flag. :thumbsup:
Jamal: I can take snapshot verification + backup TTLs. Plan: add nightly restore smoke-test on a low-cost zone, run weekly, report failures to #incidents.
Maria: I'll own runbook updates and the restore playbook dry-run during the next game day. Can we schedule the dry-run for Tue 3/10 morning?
Sylvie: @Alex, add specific checklist for Route53 health checks and low-TTL fallback policy. Keep canary to 5% traffic and circuit-break to regional-local if errors >3% for 5m.
Alex: On it. Draft checklist: 1) reduce TTL to 60s for test subdomain 2) add health-checks with 10s interval 3) route-shift automation with manual approval gate. Will paste draft shortly.
ops-bot: Automated note: created incident-ops task 4827 for "DNS canary and fallback" with blocker label.
Jamal: Backup plan: implement snapshot consistency check in restore pipeline. Pseudocode snippet:```bash
# verify latest snapshot exists
SNAP=$(aws ec2 describe-snapshots --filters Name=tag:cluster,Values=redwood-prod --query 'Snapshots[-1].SnapshotId')
aws ec2 wait snapshot-completed --snapshot-ids $SNAP
# try fast restore to t3.micro in staging-subnet
```
Nina: Heads-up from product: schedule the dry-run outside business hours if possible. We can provide coverage for feature flags.
Sylvie: Noted. Maria, can you move the dry-run to Tue 3/10 04:00 PT to minimize user impact?
Maria: Yes, 04:00 PT works. Will coordinate with infra to reserve capacity. Also adding a pre-game checklist to runbook: 1) validate KMS access, 2) validate cross-region VPC peering, 3) confirm routing policies are published.
Alex: Draft checklist posted to confluence: https://confluence/redwood/dr/dns-canary-checklist (internal). Please review before EOD Friday.
Jamal: For snapshot lag, I'll add monitoring alert (SLO: snapshot delay < 10m). If lag > 10m three times in 24h, escalate to infra rotation.
Sylvie: Ownership recap: Alex -> DNS canary & routing fallback (target 2 weeks, canary starting Mon 3/8). Jamal -> snapshot + restore smoke-tests (target in 1 week, first smoke-test by 3/5). Maria -> restore runbook + game-day dry-run (scheduled 3/10 04:00 PT). Nina -> stakeholder communication and feature-flag gating. Ops-bot -> create tracking tickets and remind owners daily at 09:00 PT.
Maria: Quick question — do we want the smoke-test to do a full data restore or a schema-only restore? Full would be safer but slower.
Jamal: Start with metadata+schemas first to keep time low, then escalate to full data restore if first two runs pass. Document both paths in runbook.
Alex: Also propose a short retro after the dry-run (30m) to capture friction points. I'll put a calendar invite.
Sylvie: Agreed. Last bit: recurring pattern triage — ops rotation to review "failover patterns" weekly and surface any new anomalies into the postmortem backlog. Can we add a recurring ticket for that?
ops-bot: Created recurring task 4890: "Weekly failover-patterns triage" assigned to oncall-rotation. First run scheduled 03/06.
Nina: Thanks. I'll send a short blurb to customers affected by last week's test and include rollback assurances.
Alex: Will open a PR for the routing automation with feature flag naming: ff/dns-canary-2026Q1.
Sylvie: Perfect. If everyone is happy with owners/times, I'll update the postmortem with these action items and mark owners as P0/P1. Reply here with any objections by EOD. :spiral_calendar:
Maria: No objections. Closing my loop after I confirm reserve capacity and update runbook.
Jamal: No objections. Starting the smoke-test work tomorrow.
Alex: No objections. Will post checklist + PR links.
Sylvie: Thanks all — I'll publish the updated action tracker after 17:00 PT and ping owners.
